scope: Theorem 12.1 (Fixed inverse-polynomial accuracy) of the manuscript “Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: L = RL = BPL” (preprints/Exact-Derandomization-of-Logarithmic-Space-L-equals-RL-equals-BPL-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 103 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 15030fab23d31a4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 92. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a randomized machine M with polynomial worst-case running time and O(log(n + 2)) work space, and fix an integer d ≥ 1. There is a uniform deterministic transducer that, on every input x of length n, outputs a dyadic rational zx ∈ [0, 1] with |zx − pM(x)| ≤ (n + 2)−d . Its work space and output length are O(log(n + 2)), and its running time is polynomial in n + 2. The constants may depend on M and d, but not on the input.
